page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 32.0 GB, yielding a high vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.0 GB per virtual core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance features a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local ephemeral storage, and lacks dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinction between single-threaded and highly parallel processing capabilities. Single-core performance falls into the bottom quartile, as demonstrated by weak stress-ng single-core (1106.89), Geekbench single-core (1001.0), and single-threaded gzip compression metrics. Conversely, multi-threaded execution metrics achieve average benchmark rankings across stress-ng multi-core (23616.79), PassMark CPU (23037.68), and Geekbench software compilation testing. Memory throughput benchmarks display average performance, topping out at 95.0 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 45.75 GB/sec for uncached writes.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the provision of 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside modest memory density suits heavily parallel, CPU-bound workloads where large per-core memory footprints are unnecessary. However, the reliance on remote storage and low single-core clock speeds present structural tradeoffs for single-threaded applications or memory-heavy databases. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded batch compilation, parallel web serving, Redis caching, microservices, and small-model LLM inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-oriented cloud instance engineered for parallel processing workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, the system features 32 dedicated vCPUs, 16 physical cores with hyper-threading, and 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache infrastructure consists of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB L3 cache, backed by a 10 Gbps baseline network interface and no local storage. Performance profiling highlights a key tradeoff: single-core metrics fall in the lower bottom quartile, whereas multi-core execution achieves average scores across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng tests. Memory bandwidth reaches 95.0 GB/sec for uncached reads. The hardware allocation offers qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded tasks that do not require large memory footprints or ephemeral local drives, making it suitable for parallel software compilation, Redis in-memory caching, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
